newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Smith confident of keeping Australia job.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Smith confident of keeping Australia job.

text.p: Australia rugby union coach Greg Smith said on Tuesday he was confident there would be no move to sack him before his contract expires in December, leaving him in charge for tours to Argentina and Britain later this year.
Smith, who took over from Bob Dwyer two years ago, has faced increasing speculation about his future in the wake of three successive defeats to New Zealand.
Asked if he was confident of leading Australia on their overseas tours in October and November, Smith told reporters: "At this stage I am".
Smith has repeatedly stated his intention to seek another stint as Wallaby coach next season.
But several media commentators have suggested key Australian Rugby Union officials favour replacing him with ACT Brumbies coach Rod Macqueen before the team leaves for South America.
Smith was speaking on the team's departure for Pretoria, where the Wallabies will face South Africa on Saturday in a Tri-Nations match that could have a significant impact on his job prospects.
Smith has recalled from injury captain and lock John Eales and flanker Matt Cockbain to face the Springboks, who were beaten 32-20 by Australia in a Tri-Nations match in Brisbane on August 2.
Eales and Cockbain, who has recovered from a mild concussion, both missed Australia's 36-24 loss to New Zealand in Dunedin on Saturday.
Eales, however, must still pass a fitness test on a knee ligament injury later in the week after playing down his chances of taking the field on Saturday.
Flanker Fili Finau and second rower John Langford, who made his test debut on Saturday, were dropped.
Smith has guided Australia to four wins in seven tests this season, including victories over France, England and South Africa to compensate for the comprehensive defeats by New Zealand.
The Wallabies will embark on a five-match tour to Argentina, including two tests against the Pumas, in late October before playing England on November 15 and Scotland two weeks later.
